title: Mock cable fingerless mitts
subtitle: Fingerless mitts with mock cable columns worked without a cable needle.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts with mock cable columns on the back of the hand, worked without a cable needle by crossing stitches on the needle. DK weight, worked in the round, afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Mock cable (cross-stitch without a cable needle) is a well-established beginner-friendly substitute for the standard cable crossing. The fingerless mitt construction follows the standard seamless DK pattern. Both elements are synthesised from published knitting techniques.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles. Mock cable rib pulls narrower; the body gauge is not affected.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cable effect created by crossing two stitches without a cable needle. On a knit cross: slip the first stitch off the needle, skip it, knit the second stitch, then catch the slipped stitch with the left needle and knit it. Produces a left or right lean without requiring a cable needle.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

A mock cable is a stitch cross worked directly on the needle without setting stitches aside on a cable needle. The cross takes about 3 seconds and the result looks like a standard 2-stitch cable. The back of the hand has two mock cable columns set into a 2x2 rib frame; the palm is plain 2x2 rib. The construction uses
on a long circular. Budget about 80 g (175 m / 190 yards) of DK wool.

content.text: 22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles. The mock cable panel will pull in slightly; this is normal and does not affect the overall circumference.

attrs.heading: RC (right cross, worked on 2 knit stitches)

items.name: Step 1
items.qty: Slip the first stitch off the left needle and let it dangle at the front of the work.

items.name: Step 2
items.qty: Knit the second stitch on the left needle.

items.name: Step 3
items.qty: Pick up the dangling stitch with the left needle tip from the front, and knit it.

content.text: This creates a right-leaning cross. Work the cross every 4 rounds to create an unbroken spiral column. The dangling stitch sits at the front very briefly; keep your grip steady and do not let it drop to the floor.

attrs.heading: Round types for the hand section

items.name: Cross round
items.qty: Palm: k2, p2 rib for 20 (22, 24) sts. Back: p2, RC, p2, k6, p2, RC, p2.

items.name: Plain rounds 2-4
items.qty: Palm: k2, p2 rib. Back: p2, k2, p2, k6, p2, k2, p2.

content.text: Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. The back of the hand sits on the first 20 (22, 24) stitches and the palm on the second 20 (22, 24). Join to work in the round. Work 20 (22, 24) rounds of 2x2 rib.
Set up the mock cable panel on the back stitches: p2, k2, p2, k6, p2, k2, p2. Continue the 4-round cross pattern for 10 (12, 12) rounds.

On the next plain palm round: work the first 10 (11, 12) palm stitches with waste yarn, slip back, work in pattern to end. Continue the mock cable pattern for 16 (18, 20) more rounds. Bind off in pattern.
Remove waste yarn. Pick up 10 (11, 12) stitches above and below the gap. Work 12 (14, 14) rounds of 1x1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Dropped dangling stitch: the needle tip let the stitch fall from the front when reaching for the second stitch. Slow down and let the stitch sit close to the tip before knitting the second stitch.

Cross goes the wrong way: the cross was worked right-to-left instead of following the instructions. The dangling stitch must sit at the front of the fabric (not the back) to produce a right-leaning cross.
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Block the mitts to open the mock cable columns.
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry.
The cabled fingerless mitts pattern uses a real cable needle and a 4-stitch cable panel. The mock cable here is an equivalent look at beginner level.
